questions.stem: Which teaching about sublingual nitroglycerin should the nurse give? Select all that apply.

options.text: Take one tablet under the tongue at the start of pain
Call 911 if pain is not better 5 minutes after the first tablet
Keep tablets in the original dark glass bottle
A headache means the tablets are dangerous; stop them

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed. Isosorbide mononitrate each morning. Metoprolol.

questions.stem: Before giving metoprolol in the clinic, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give the dose because angina is the priority
Tell the client to stop metoprolol at home suddenly

rationale.correct: Bradycardia means hold and notify; never stop beta blockers suddenly.

questions.stem: Because of the kidney function, the provider switches to denosumab every 6 months. Which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

caseStudies.title: Stable angina drugs and a nitrate interaction

exhibits.title: Cardiology clinic
exhibits.body: A 62-year-old client has chest pressure when climbing stairs that goes away with rest in 5 minutes. The client was prescribed sublingual nitroglycerin, metoprolol and isosorbide mononitrate. The client asks whether sildenafil from a friend is safe.

caseStudies.title: Osteoporosis drugs from alendronate to denosumab

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 70-year-old client started alendronate 70 mg weekly a month ago. The client takes it at bedtime with milk and lies down. The client now has burning chest pain when swallowing.

caseStudies.title: H. pylori ulcer and long-term PPI effects

exhibits.title: GI clinic
exhibits.body: A 58-year-old client has had burning upper abdominal pain that improves with food for 2 months and black stools twice. The client has taken omeprazole for 6 years for reflux and ibuprofen for back pain.

exhibits.title: Day 1 after bowel surgery
exhibits.body: A 24-year-old client has nausea after surgery. Ondansetron was given twice, metoclopramide 10 mg IV an hour ago, and promethazine was ordered IV push through a hand IV.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
